current_recipes.title: Egg Kidney Beans Spinach Breakfast Wrap

method: Get the pan to a medium-high heat and prepare the filling first. Cook the large eggs until just set, keeping it tender rather than hammering it dry.
Add the vegetables and cook until softened but still with a bit of bite. Stir the measured sauce or seasoning through for the final 30–60 seconds so it coats the filling rather than burning.
Warm the wrap for 20–30 seconds so it bends without splitting. Put the filling just below the centre, fold the sides in and roll it up firmly.
For a better finish, put the wrapped seam-side down in the dry pan for a minute to seal and lightly crisp it. Eat while hot.

current_recipes.title: Chicken Slow Cooker Stew

ingredients.item: reduced-salt vegetable stock cube (make up to 250ml with water)

method: If you have five minutes, brown the chicken breast in a properly hot pan first. It is optional, but that bit of colour gives the finished dish far more depth.
Put the vegetables, measured cooking liquid and chicken breast into the slow cooker. Stir once so everything is coated, then cook on LOW for 6–8 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours.

Keep the lid on while it cooks. In the final 30 minutes, check the texture: if the cooking liquid is still thin, leave the lid slightly ajar or finish uncovered where your cooker allows until it reduces.
Check the chicken breast is safely cooked, taste the finished dish and adjust the seasoning before serving. Cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate.

current_recipes.title: Shift Balti Beef Traybake

method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the baby potatoes into even pieces, toss with the measured oil and get them roasting first for 15 minutes so they actually have time to colour.
While they start, prepare the vegetables and 5% beef mince. Get the pan properly hot first. Cook the 5% beef mince until browned and cooked through — colour is flavour, so do not crowd the pan.

Add the vegetables to the hot tray and roast for another 15–20 minutes. Stir the measured sauce through near the end rather than drowning everything at the start; you want roasted edges, not steamed dinner.
Check the 5% beef mince is properly cooked and the potatoes are golden and tender. Let the tray sit for 2 minutes, taste, season if it needs it, then serve.

current_recipes.title: Shift Hash Brown Bacon Breakfast Buttie

method: Peel the baby potatoes and weigh 120g of the raw peeled flesh, then dice it into roughly 1cm pieces. Peel and finely grate the measured 20g onion, chop the 90g tomato, and wash the 90g spinach. Keep raw-meat preparation separate from these vegetables.

Put the diced potatoes into a saucepan of boiling water. Simmer for about 8–10 minutes until a fork passes easily through the centre. Drain thoroughly in a colander, leave to steam dry for 2 minutes, then roughly mash with a fork. Mix in the finely grated onion and press into two small, thin potato patties, about 1cm thick.

Heat 6ml of the measured 10ml olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the potato patties for about 6–8 minutes on each side, turning carefully with a wide spatula, until golden and crisp and the onion is soft. Lower the heat if they darken before the onion cooks. While they cook, prepare the protein and vegetables in the second pan using the steps below. Keep the finished patties warm on a clean plate until assembly.

Trim visible fat and weigh the listed 90g bacon raw, then cut into bite-size pieces. In the second frying pan, use 2ml of the measured olive oil and cook over a medium heat, turning for about 6–8 minutes until fully cooked. Check the thickest part with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C and remain there for 2 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate while the vegetables cook.

In the second frying pan, heat 2ml of the measured oil over a medium heat. Cook the chopped tomato for 3–4 minutes until softened, then add the spinach and stir until wilted. Return the cooked protein and its juices to the vegetables just before assembling, keeping everything hot.

Split and toast the measured 80g wholemeal bap. Put one crisp potato patty and a manageable amount of hot protein and vegetables inside. Serve the second patty and all remaining filling alongside; the nutrition includes the complete listed portion.
Serve immediately while the potato is crisp. For preparing ahead, follow the component storage instructions; assemble only when ready to eat.

storage.reheat: Reheat chilled cooked components once only until steaming hot throughout, then assemble and eat immediately.

current_recipes.title: Shift Katsu Salmon Fakeaway Kebab

method: Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Warm the wholemeal flatbread in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–60 seconds on each side, until flexible. Keep it covered on a clean plate.

Check the salmon fillet for pin bones and pat it dry. Keep it as a fillet for cooking. After handling raw salmon fillet, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon over a medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on the first side and 3–4 minutes on the other; start skin-side down if it has skin. Turn with a wide spatula. Check the thickest part: the fish should be opaque through the centre and separate readily into flakes. Keep cooking if the centre is translucent.

Put the measured katsu-style sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.
Put the lettuce and tomato on the warm flatbread. Add large flakes of the cooked salmon and the warm sauce, fold the bread around the filling and serve immediately.

Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Warm the wholemeal flatbread in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–60 seconds on each side, until flexible. Keep it covered on a clean plate.

Press the turkey breast mince firmly into three short koftas, each no thicker than 1.5cm; no skewers or binder are needed. Coat with all the measured paprika, chilli powder, garlic powder and dried oregano. After handling raw turkey breast mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the turkey koftas over a medium heat for about 10–12 minutes, turning them onto every side. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato on the warm flatbread. Add the cooked turkey koftas, fold the bread around the filling and serve immediately.

Mix the measured light mayonnaise, tomato ketchup and wholegrain mustard in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Slice the chicken breast horizontally into cutlets about 1.5cm thick so they cook evenly and fit the bun. After handling raw chicken breast, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the chicken cutlets over a medium heat for about 5–6 minutes on each side, lowering the heat if they brown too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato in the toasted bun, add the cooked chicken cutlets and the cold finishing sauce, then close the bun and serve immediately.

current_recipes.title: Shift Smoky Chilli Turkey Proper Curry

method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.

Start the 75g basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Peel and finely slice the 90g onion and deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Keep the 170g turkey breast mince chilled until the pan is ready. Do not rinse raw mince.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the turkey breast mince, break it into small pieces with a spatula and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring until no raw clumps remain and it is steaming hot throughout. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g onion and 90g mixed peppers and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g smoked chilli tomato sauce. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Return the cooked turkey breast mince and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Serve immediately.

method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.

Start the 75g basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Peel and finely slice the 90g onion and deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Keep the 170g turkey breast mince chilled until the pan is ready. Do not rinse raw mince.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the turkey breast mince, break it into small pieces with a spatula and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring until no raw clumps remain and it is steaming hot throughout. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g onion and 90g mixed peppers and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g tikka masala sauce. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Return the cooked turkey breast mince and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Serve immediately.

current_recipes.title: Shift Garlic & Herb Beef Rice Bowl

method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 75g basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Peel and finely slice the 90g onion and deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Keep the 160g 5% beef mince chilled until the pan is ready. Do not rinse raw mince.
Mix 20g light mayonnaise, 1g garlic powder and 1g dried parsley in a small bowl. Keep this dressing cold until serving; it is not a cooking sauce and must not be simmered in the pan.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the 5% beef mince, break it into small pieces with a spatula and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring until no raw clumps remain and it is steaming hot throughout. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g onion and 90g mixed peppers and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.

Return the cooked 5% beef mince and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Take the pan off the heat and spoon the cold dressing over each serving; do not return it to the hob. Serve immediately.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Cook the measured dry wholewheat pasta in boiling water for 2 minutes less than its packet time. Drain, saving a small cup of cooking water.

Dice the courgette. Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat with 2 tablespoons of water; no oil is listed for this recipe. Pat the firm tofu dry, cut into 2cm cubes and cook over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, turning until the edges are golden and the middle is hot. Add another spoonful of water if needed to prevent sticking, then transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.
Add the courgette, chopped tomatoes and 3 tablespoons of pasta cooking water to the pan. Cover and simmer for 6–8 minutes until the courgette softens, then remove the lid.
Fold in the drained pasta and cooked firm tofu. Transfer to a small ovenproof dish and scatter over the measured reduced-fat cheddar.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the cheese melts and the centre is bubbling and steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.

current_recipes.title: Chicken Chilli

method: The listed brown rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 70g dry brown rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.

Drain and rinse canned, ready-cooked kidney beans, then weigh out 100g; raw or dried kidney beans cannot be used in this method. Cut the 170g chicken breast into pieces no larger than 2cm on a separate board. Wash hands, the board and knife after handling the raw meat; do not rinse it.

Warm a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat; this recipe does not include frying oil. Add the chicken breast in one layer and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning regularly. Lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Put the 120g chopped tomatoes and 5g smoked paprika into the same frying pan. Stir over a medium-low heat, then cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir twice; keep the heat low enough that the tomato liquid does not boil dry.
Add the drained kidney beans, cover and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring halfway, until the beans are hot through.

Return the cooked chicken breast and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat everything together over a low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring gently, until steaming hot throughout. Spoon over the freshly cooked rice and serve immediately.

Start the 70g dry basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Wash and drain the 100g spinach. Cut the 170g turkey breast into pieces no larger than 2cm on a separate board. Wash hands, the board and knife after handling the raw meat; do not rinse it.

Warm a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat; this recipe does not include frying oil. Add the turkey breast in one layer and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning regularly. Lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Put the 120g chopped tomatoes and 25g medium curry paste into the same frying pan. Stir over a medium-low heat, then cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir twice; keep the heat low enough that the tomato liquid does not boil dry.
Add the washed spinach in two handfuls, cover for 1 minute, then stir. Cook for another 2–3 minutes until wilted throughout.

Return the cooked turkey breast and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat everything together over a low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring gently, until steaming hot throughout. Spoon over the freshly cooked rice and serve immediately.

method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel and cut the potatoes into even 2cm chunks. Boil for 15–20 minutes until a knife goes through easily, then drain and mash with 2–3 tablespoons of the hot cooking water; no milk or butter is added.
Dice the carrots finely. Measure the balti-style sauce ready to add near the end of cooking.

Heat half the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Add the 5% beef mince, break it into small pieces with a spoon and fry over medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes. Keep turning until browned and steaming hot throughout; check the centre reaches 75°C for 30 seconds with a clean thermometer. Transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.

Add the remaining measured olive oil, carrots and 60ml water to the pan. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the carrots soften; add the peas for the final 3 minutes and cook until piping hot. Add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the carrots are tender.
Return the cooked filling to the vegetables. Stir in the balti-style sauce, heat for 1–2 minutes, then spoon into a small ovenproof dish.

Spread the mashed potato over the filling and roughen the top with a fork. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the top colours and the centre of the pie is steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve while hot.

method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel and cut the potatoes into even 2cm chunks. Boil for 15–20 minutes until a knife goes through easily, then drain and mash with 2–3 tablespoons of the hot cooking water; no milk or butter is added.
Dice the carrots finely. Measure the peri-peri sauce ready to add near the end of cooking.

Heat half the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cut the chicken breast into even 2cm pieces. Fry over medium-high heat for about 8–12 minutes, turning regularly. Cook until no pink remains inside and the pieces are steaming hot throughout; a clean thermometer should read 75°C for 30 seconds at the centre. Transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.

Add the remaining measured olive oil, carrots and 60ml water to the pan. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the carrots soften; add the peas for the final 3 minutes and cook until piping hot. Add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the carrots are tender.

Spread the mashed potato over the filling and roughen the top with a fork. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the top colours and the centre of the pie is steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve while hot.

Dice the carrots finely. Stir together the measured light mayonnaise, garlic powder, dried parsley in a small bowl and keep this dressing chilled until serving.

Heat half the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cut the lean pork loin into even 2cm pieces. Fry over medium-high heat for about 8–12 minutes, turning regularly. Cook until no pink remains inside and the pieces are steaming hot throughout; a clean thermometer should read 75°C for 30 seconds at the centre. Transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.

Add the remaining measured olive oil, carrots and 60ml water to the pan. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the carrots soften; add the peas for the final 3 minutes and cook until piping hot. Add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the carrots are tender.
Return the cooked filling to the vegetables. Keep the chilled dressing separate for serving; spoon the hot filling into a small ovenproof dish.

Spread the mashed potato over the filling and roughen the top with a fork. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the top colours and the centre of the pie is steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve the light mayonnaise, garlic powder, dried parsley dressing alongside.

current_recipes.title: Shift Peppercorn Salmon Proper Pie

method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel and cut the potatoes into even 2cm chunks. Boil for 15–20 minutes until a knife goes through easily, then drain and mash with 2–3 tablespoons of the hot cooking water; no milk or butter is added.
Dice the carrots finely. Stir together the measured light mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard, black pepper in a small bowl and keep this dressing chilled until serving.

Heat half the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon fillet separately over medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on each side, adjusting for thickness, until the centre is opaque and flakes easily. Lift onto a clean plate and break into large flakes, checking for bones. Transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.

Add the remaining measured olive oil, carrots and 60ml water to the pan. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the carrots soften; add the peas for the final 3 minutes and cook until piping hot. Add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the carrots are tender.
Return the cooked filling to the vegetables. Keep the chilled dressing separate for serving; spoon the hot filling into a small ovenproof dish.

Spread the mashed potato over the filling and roughen the top with a fork. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the top colours and the centre of the pie is steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve the light mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard, black pepper dressing alongside.

current_recipes.title: Shift BBQ Beef Proper Pizza

method: Weigh the individual pizza base before cooking, using the raw weight listed in the ingredients. Preheat the oven to the temperature stated on its packet. Put a baking tray inside to heat. Keep the base ready on a board; follow any packet instruction to pre-bake it, and use its stated baking time for the final oven stage.
Slice the mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and cook the peppers for 5–6 minutes until softened; transfer them to a clean bowl.

Keep the 5% beef mince ready to break into small pieces in the pan. After handling raw 5% beef mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the beef mince over a medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes, breaking up clumps and stirring until browned. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.

Transfer the cooked beef mince to the bowl of peppers. Add the measured tomato passata to the empty frying pan and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened so it will not soak the base.

Put the measured reduced-sugar BBQ sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.

Spread all the thickened tomato passata over the individual pizza base, leaving a narrow border. Arrange the cooked peppers and the cooked beef mince evenly on top, then spoon over the warm sauce. Carefully slide onto the hot tray.
Bake for the pizza base packet's stated time, until the dough is cooked through, the base is crisp underneath and the topping is hot throughout. Rest for one minute, cut and serve.

method: Weigh the individual pizza base before cooking, using the raw weight listed in the ingredients. Preheat the oven to the temperature stated on its packet. Put a baking tray inside to heat. Keep the base ready on a board; follow any packet instruction to pre-bake it, and use its stated baking time for the final oven stage.
Slice the mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and cook the peppers for 5–6 minutes until softened; transfer them to a clean bowl.
Cut the chicken breast into strips about 1.5cm thick. After handling raw chicken breast, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the chicken strips over a medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes, turning regularly so every side colours. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.

Transfer the cooked chicken strips to the bowl of peppers. Add the measured tomato passata to the empty frying pan and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened so it will not soak the base.

Put the measured katsu-style sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.

Spread all the thickened tomato passata over the individual pizza base, leaving a narrow border. Arrange the cooked peppers and the cooked chicken strips evenly on top, then spoon over the warm sauce. Carefully slide onto the hot tray.
Bake for the pizza base packet's stated time, until the dough is cooked through, the base is crisp underneath and the topping is hot throughout. Rest for one minute, cut and serve.

current_recipes.title: Shift Katsu Salmon Loaded Fries

method: Use plain, uncoated oven-ready chips without batter. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.

Check the salmon fillet for pin bones and pat it dry. Keep it as a fillet for cooking. After handling raw salmon fillet, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon over a medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on the first side and 3–4 minutes on the other; start skin-side down if it has skin. Turn with a wide spatula. Check the thickest part: the fish should be opaque through the centre and separate readily into flakes. Keep cooking if the centre is translucent.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot. Keep the salmon in large flakes rather than mashing it.

Put the measured katsu-style sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.
Pile the crisp oven chips onto a plate and spoon over large flakes of the cooked salmon, the red onion and peppers, followed by the warm sauce. Serve immediately while the chips are crisp.

Serve the cooked 5% beef mince, roast potatoes, carrots and broccoli together. Spoon the hot reduced-sugar BBQ glaze over the cooked protein.

current_recipes.title: Shift BBQ Beef Loaded Fries

method: Use plain, uncoated oven-ready chips without batter. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.

Keep the 5% beef mince ready to break into small pieces in the pan. After handling raw 5% beef mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the beef mince over a medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes, breaking up clumps and stirring until browned. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot.

Put the measured reduced-sugar BBQ sauce into a small saucepan. Warm over a low heat, stirring, for about 2–3 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout; follow a longer cooking time on the sauce label. Keep warm for serving.
Pile the crisp oven chips onto a plate and spoon over the cooked beef mince, the red onion and peppers, followed by the warm sauce. Serve immediately while the chips are crisp.

method: Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.

Use plain, uncoated oven-ready chips without batter. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.

Keep the turkey breast mince ready to break into small pieces in the pan. After handling raw turkey breast mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot.

method: Weigh the individual pizza base before cooking, using the raw weight listed in the ingredients. Preheat the oven to the temperature stated on its packet. Put a baking tray inside to heat. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.

Check the salmon fillet for pin bones and pat it dry. Keep it as a fillet for cooking. Coat with all the measured salt and black pepper. After handling raw salmon fillet, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon over a medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on the first side and 3–4 minutes on the other; start skin-side down if it has skin. Turn with a wide spatula. Check the thickest part: the fish should be opaque through the centre and separate readily into flakes. Keep cooking if the centre is translucent.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot. Keep the salmon in large flakes rather than mashing it.
Pile the crisp oven chips onto a plate and spoon over large flakes of the cooked salmon, the red onion and peppers. Serve immediately while the chips are crisp.

current_recipes.title: Shift Classic Beef Loaded Fries

method: Use plain, uncoated oven-ready chips without batter. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise, tomato ketchup and wholegrain mustard in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Keep the 5% beef mince ready to break into small pieces in the pan. After handling raw 5% beef mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the beef mince over a medium-high heat for about 8–10 minutes, breaking up clumps and stirring until browned. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot.

Pile the crisp oven chips onto a plate and spoon over the cooked beef mince, the red onion and peppers. Drizzle the cold finishing sauce over the top after cooking. Serve immediately while the chips are crisp.

Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise, tomato ketchup and wholegrain mustard in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Check the salmon fillet for pin bones and pat it dry. Keep it as a fillet for cooking. After handling raw salmon fillet, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the salmon over a medium heat for about 4–5 minutes on the first side and 3–4 minutes on the other; start skin-side down if it has skin. Turn with a wide spatula. method: The listed 75g dry egg noodles is an uncooked weight. Cut the 90g broccoli into small florets. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, cook the broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then lift it onto a plate with a slotted spoon. Cook the noodles in the same boiling water for the time on their packet until tender, then drain well. Time this to finish shortly before the pan ingredients are ready.
Deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Keep the 160g 5% beef mince chilled until the pan is ready. Do not rinse raw mince.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the 5% beef mince, break it into small pieces with a spatula and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring until no raw clumps remain and it is steaming hot throughout. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g mixed peppers and cook for 4–6 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.
Add the drained noodles and broccoli to the pan. Toss gently for 1–2 minutes to combine without crushing the florets.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g balti-style sauce. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Return the cooked 5% beef mince and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Divide the noodles, vegetables and 5% beef mince between serving bowls. Serve immediately.

method: Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.

The listed 75g dry egg noodles is an uncooked weight. Cut the 90g broccoli into small florets. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, cook the broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then lift it onto a plate with a slotted spoon. Start the 75g brown rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.

Deseed and dice the 90g red pepper and drain and rinse canned, ready-cooked kidney beans, then weigh out 90g; raw or dried kidney beans cannot be used in this method. Check the 150g salmon fillet for bones. Keep it as a fillet for pan cooking, then flake it after cooking.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Put in the salmon fillet, skin-side down if it has skin. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turn carefully and cook for another 3–5 minutes until the centre is opaque, steaming hot and flakes easily; a thicker piece needs longer. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g red pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.
Add the drained kidney beans. Cover and heat for 3–4 minutes over a low heat, stirring halfway, until the beans are steaming hot.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g pepper and tomato masala. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Flake the cooked salmon into large pieces and fold into the pan at the end; avoid breaking it up with vigorous stirring. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, folding carefully so the seafood stays intact. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Serve immediately.

Start the 75g brown rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.

Deseed and dice the 90g red pepper and drain and rinse canned, ready-cooked kidney beans, then weigh out 90g; raw or dried kidney beans cannot be used in this method. Keep the 160g 5% beef mince chilled until the pan is ready. Do not rinse raw mince.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the 5% beef mince, break it into small pieces with a spatula and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring until no raw clumps remain and it is steaming hot throughout. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g red pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.
Add the drained kidney beans. Cover and heat for 3–4 minutes over a low heat, stirring halfway, until the beans are steaming hot.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g reduced-sugar BBQ glaze. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Return the cooked 5% beef mince and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Serve immediately.
